sentences.text:
This appeal is filed by the claimants/appellants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') challenging the judgment and award dated 08.04.2019 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-II, Yadgir, (for short hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.190/2017.
2.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-II, Yadgir
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
Appellants are the petitioners and the respondents are the respondents before the Tribunal.

3. Facts giving rise to filing of this appeal are that, on 25.07.2017 the deceased-Konda Rajshekar was proceeding on Glamour motorcycle bearing registration No.AP-22/AA-2901 towards Makthal from Krishna on Krishna-Nallu Gattu Maremma Temple road on the extreme left side of the main road.

At about 2.30 p.m., NC: 2024:KHC-K:3859-DB when he was near Gudeballur village, driver of lorry bearing registration No.KA-25/AA-3559 drove the lorry in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the deceased.
Due to which, Rajshekar fell down, sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
It is contended that the deceased was aged about 42 years as on the date of the accident and was earning Rs.3,59,926/- per annum.

The petitioners being the legal representatives of the deceased-Konda Rajshekar have filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Act claiming compensation on account of the death of Konda Rajshekar.
4. Respondent No.2 filed objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
5. The Tribunal on the basis of the pleadings of the parties framed the issues.
In order to prove the contents of the claim petition, petitioner No.1 was examined as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents as NC: 2024:KHC-K:3859-DB Exs.P1 to P15.
The respondents have not led any oral evidence, but they have got marked two documents as Exs.
R1 and R2.

6. The Tribunal, after recording the evidence, hearing both side and on assessment of the oral and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.33,42,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
7. The petitioners/appellants, being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, have preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the deceased-Konda Rajshekar was doing business and was earning Rs.3,59,926/- per annum.
He submits that in order to establish that he was doing business and he was income-tax assessee, the petitioners have produced copies of the income tax returns which are marked as Exs.P10 to P12.
He submits that the Tribunal has taken average of three years and assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.3,38,231/- per annum.
He submits that the Tribunal ought to have taken the income for the assessment year 2016-17 which is Rs.3,59,926/- per annum.
In order to buttress his arguments, he has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Shashikala and others vs. Gangalakshmamma and another reported in (2015)9 SCC 150.

entities.text: Shashikala and others vs. Gangalakshmamma and another reported in (2015)9 SCC 150
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that the Tribunal has not added future prospects to the income of the deceased as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay NC: 2024:KHC-K:3859-DB Sethi and Others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay NC: 2024:KHC-K:3859-DB Sethi and Others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal.

10. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supports the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for interference.
On these grounds, he prays to dismiss the appeal.

11. Perused the records and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
12.
The point that arises for our consideration is with regard to quantum of compensation.
13. It is not in dispute that the deceased-Konda Rajshekar met with accident and he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

In order to establish that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioners have produced certified copy of the FIR marked NC: 2024:KHC-K:3859-DB as Ex.P1 and charge sheet marked as Ex.P5.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in recording finding that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

14. Insofar as quantum of compensation, it is the case of the petitioners that the deceased-Konda Rajshekar was doing business and he was income tax assessee and the petitioners have produced copies of the income tax returns of three years i.e., 2014-2015, 2015-2016 and 2016-2017 wherein the gross income of the deceased is shown as Rs.3,05,041/-, Rs.3,49,728/- and Rs.3,59,926/-
respectively.
But, the Tribunal has taken the average of the same which comes to Rs.3,38,231/-.
The Tribunal could have taken the income of the deceased as per Ex.P12 for the assessment year 2016-2017.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Shashikala (supra) held that the Tribunal has to consider the income of the deceased as per the last income tax returns.
In the instant case, the Tribunal has taken the average of three years income and NC: 2024:KHC-K:3859-DB assessed the income at Rs.3,38,231/- per annum.
Thus, considering Ex.P12, it is just and proper to consider the gross income of the deceased at Rs.3,59,926/- per annum.

As per the income tax slab, tax is exempted upto Rs.2,50,000/- and for the income above Rs.2,50,000/- (Rs.3,59,926-Rs.2,50,000 =
Rs.1,09,926/-), 10% tax has to be deducted (Rs.1,09,926/- x 10%=Rs.10,993).
After deducting income-tax of 10%, it comes to Rs.3,48,933/- (Rs.3,59,926-Rs.10,993).

Thus, we re-assess the Kavitha And Ors vs The Managing Partner And Anr on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93762721/
4 income of the deceased at Rs.3,48,933/- per annum.

entities.text: Kavitha And Ors vs The Managing Partner And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To the aforesaid amount, as the deceased was aged 42 years, 25% of the said amount has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
Thus, the income comes to Rs.4,36,166/-.
After excluding claimant No.4, there are three claimants.
Hence, 1/3rd of the said income has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased which comes to Rs.2,90,777/- (Rs.4,36,166/- - Rs.1,45,389/-).

Taking into account the age of the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3859-DB deceased which was 42 years at the time of accident, multiplier of 14 has to be adopted as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009)6 SCC 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,70,878/- (Rs.2,90,777x14) on account of loss of dependency.

15. Further, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) and Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram &
Others reported in (2018)18 SCC 130, each petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards loss of consortium.

entities.text:
Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram &
Others reported in (2018)18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners are three in number, hence, the compensation towards loss of consortium would be Rs.1,32,000/- (44,000x3).
In addition, the petitioners/ appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- towards funeral and transportation expenses.
Petitioner No.3 is the father and petitioner No.4 is the sister of the deceased and they are not heirs in class-I of Schedule of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.

Hence, the Tribunal was justified in not awarding compensation to petitioner Nos.3 and 4.
17.
Thus, in all, petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.42,35,878/- as against Rs.33,42,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

18. In view of the above discussion, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
iii. Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are entitled to total compensation of Rs.42,35,878/- as against Rs.33,42,000/-.
